senses.sense_definition: To pour a liquid from one container into another

examples.text: It is best to <w>decant</w> the wine into a glass carafe before serving it to guests.
You should <w>decant</w> the juice into a clean pitcher to keep it fresh in the refrigerator.

senses.sense_definition: To pour a liquid slowly to leave sediment behind

examples.text: The chemist had to carefully <w>decant</w> the solution to separate the clear liquid from the solid particles.
Wait for the mixture to settle completely before you <w>decant</w> the clear top layer into a new beaker.

senses.sense_definition: To temporarily move people out of their homes during building renovations

examples.text: The council had to <w>decant</w> all the residents while the apartment block underwent major structural repairs.
Many families were <w>decanted</w> into temporary housing while their original homes were being modernized.

senses.sense_definition: To remove an artificially gestated being from its growth chamber

examples.text: In the science fiction novel, the laboratory technicians <w>decant</w> the infants from their artificial wombs.
The process to <w>decant</w> the clones must be performed under strictly controlled environmental conditions.

senses.sense_definition: To flow or discharge into another body of water

examples.text: The small mountain stream continues to <w>decant</w> into the larger river further down the valley.
The runoff from the melting snow will <w>decant</w> into the lake during the spring thaw.
